rms_audit.device: salt1 HCU cuda:0, BF16 NS, lr=1.5625e-4, momentum=0.95, fixed grad snapshot

metric_definition.old: update_rms_per_group = single-step actual parameter-delta RMS = RMS(p_after - p_before), momentum from 0, 1st step, element-weighted within group (sqrt(sum(d^2)/n)).
metric_definition.verdict: definition is CONSISTENT and CORRECT (not relative RMS, not momentum RMS, not mixed across groups). The non-uniformity was real (NS divergence), not a telemetry/aggregation bug.

moonlight_invariant.theory: Moonlight factor 0.2*sqrt(max(d_in,d_out)) cancels the 1/sqrt(max(dim)) RMS of the semi-orthogonal (polar) NS output, so scaled_pre_lr_rms ~= 0.2 (shape-independent) and applied delta RMS ~= 0.2*lr.
moonlight_invariant.invariant_pass: HOLDS for all shapes where NS converges (q/content_gate/attn_out/ffn = 0.19-0.22). BROKEN only where NS diverges (k/v=69-73, adaln=9.1) because the NS output is no longer orthogonalized. Confirms the math is correct; the non-uniformity is NS divergence, not Moonlight.

chunked_concat_verification.note: custom CMuon chunked (split->per-chunk NS->concat) vs concat of INDEPENDENT native Muon per chunk. RMS rel-diff <2% on all cases (same order as single-shape BF16 matmul non-determinism) -> chunking logic CORRECT. max_abs_diff~2.4e-4 is NS-iteration amplification of BF16 matmul non-determinism at outlier elements, NOT a chunking bug.

ns_convergence_window.note: per-iteration NS output RMS (polar = 1/sqrt(max) is the converged target). The 5th iteration leaves the convergence basin for small-short-edge shapes.

ns5_vs_ns6_classification.task5_A_or_B: A (native AND custom both diverge) -> HCU/BF16/shape numerical phenomenon of the quintic NS, NOT a CMuon implementation bug (task5-B would be native-stable/custom-divergent).
ns5_vs_ns6_classification.note: ns5 already diverges for k/v[640,2560] & adaln[2560,1024] (not only ns6). The old report's 'ns5 stable, ns6 diverges' was wrong.

rms_audit.root_cause: The quintic Newton-Schulz iteration has a shape-dependent convergence window that depends on the largest singular value after Frobenius pre-normalization (~ 1/sqrt(c) + 1/sqrt(r) for wide [r,c]). Shapes with a small short edge (k/v short=640, adaln short=1024) have a larger max singular value (>~0.045) and leave the convergence basin at iteration 5; larger-short-edge shapes (q/ffn short>=2560) converge at iteration 5 and only diverge at iteration 6. This is identical in native torch.optim.Muon (NS function is line-identical, Moonlight == adjust_lr_fn='match_rms_adamw').
rms_audit.ns4_is_safe: ns4 lands inside the convergence window for ALL production shapes: delta RMS ~= 0.2*lr (q 2.78e-5 / k 4.87e-5 / adaln 3.42e-5 / ffn 3.17e-5). Recommended: switch cmuon_ns_steps 5->4 and re-measure.
